page: Microsoft Azure M1pds_v4 is an ARM-based, memory-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provides 1 dedicated vCPU built on 64-bit ARM architecture (arm64) and is equipped with 16.0 GB of memory. This architecture establishes a high memory-to-compute ratio of 16 GB per core, targeting environments that prioritize RAM allocation over parallel CPU execution.

Storage configuration includes an integrated 59 GB local NVMe SSD, alongside compatibility with Azure Premium Storage volumes for expanded block storage requirements. The instance features no discrete graphics processing units (0 GPU count) and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring standard cloud networking constructs for external ingress.

Because the M1pds_v4 pairs an energy-efficient ARM core with a generous memory allocation, it offers cost-effective resource density for services requiring memory footprints that exceed standard general-purpose profiles. Primary tradeoffs center on compute density, as workloads are limited to a single dedicated thread. This hardware configuration is suited for low-concurrency in-memory caching systems, lightweight relational databases, Redis key-value stores, ARM64 development nodes, and memory-dependent background workers.
description: Microsoft Azure M1pds_v4 is an ARM-based, memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features a single dedicated vCPU based on 64-bit ARM architecture paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:16 compute-to-memory ratio. Local ephemeral storage is provided via a 59 GB NVMe SSD, alongside support for Azure Premium Storage. The configuration contains no discrete GPU hardware accelerators. By utilizing ARM architecture with a high memory allocation per core, the M1pds_v4 delivers strong resource efficiency for applications that demand significant memory capacity without the overhead of excess compute cores. It is suited for workloads such as memory-resident caching, small-scale transactional databases, ARM64 development environments, and data pre-processing pipelines with modest thread concurrency requirements.
